summary.headline: Restaurant Brands Asia Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20% to ₹844 crore; company-level EBITDA jumped 281% to ₹43.2 crore, India SSSG 14%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 20% YoY to ₹844 crore and restaurant-level EBITDA rose to about ₹92 crore (up 73%). India SSSG was 14% with ADS of ₹1.31 lakh, and India company-level EBITDA reached ₹55 crore at 7.8% of revenue (versus ₹28 crore a year earlier). Indonesia revenue was ₹139 crore, with restaurant EBITDA marginally positive and company-level loss narrowing to ₹12 crore. Management said the restaurant EBITDA margin has hovered near 13% and expects it to move toward 15% through volume growth; gross margin dipped about 0.4 points on chicken cost headwinds. A Families pillar was added and Indonesia's Super Hemat value programme was launched in late September.

financial_highlights.change: second consecutive quarter of strong growth; prior quarter 12.6%

segments.name: India (Burger King)
segments.commentary: 607 restaurants in 144 cities at quarter end (619 opened as of call date), contributing 83% of revenue; SSSG 14% and company-level EBITDA ₹55 crore. Growth is traffic-led, with 14 consecutive quarters of positive dine-in traffic.

segments.name: Indonesia Burger King
segments.commentary: 137 restaurants; management says it has been restaurant-EBITDA positive for three consecutive quarters. Super Hemat added about 35-40 traffic per restaurant per day, and BK ADT growth is cited at about 35.

segments.name: Indonesia Popeyes
segments.commentary: 25 restaurants; ADS fell to ₹64,000 last quarter and revenue was about ₹15 crore. Restaurant-level EBITDA is weak, and management is in talks with brand owners on a resolution.

guidance_outlook: Restaurant EBITDA expected to hover around 13% now and move toward 15% as volumes build; no near-term guidance on Q3/Q4 SSSG beyond a 'very happy' start to the quarter.
India expansion to accelerate from roughly 50-70 openings a year toward 80-100 restaurants in future; 12 stores opened in October.
Indonesia: no new Burger King store growth planned in 2026 or 2027; focus on asset upgrades, profitability and a target of +₹5 million IDR daily ADS per restaurant.
Up to ₹130 crore primary capital for Indonesia to be drawn in tranches tied to milestones; board approval being sought.
Warrants could bring about ₹450 crore more cash; current liquidity cited at about ₹1,000 crore.
capex_capacity: India has 607 restaurants at quarter end and 619 by call date; pipeline now built 6-8 quarters ahead with a more linear opening cadence.
India energy-efficiency work (solar, HVAC, lighting) is being transferred to Indonesia, with significant changes targeted by end-November and most by March.
Indonesia asset upgrade (HVAC, kitchen equipment, front-of-house) runs for about the next six months.
Indonesia SOK kiosk installations to complete by March.
Cluster approach around DCs is cutting distribution costs in some markets.
demand_pricing: India growth is driven by traffic, not check; management says check has been roughly flat for many quarters, and pricing is expected to track the industry's 4-5% annual increase.
Value programme 2 for ₹79 / ₹99 on app; app frequency up about 7% YoY.
Korean Season 2 delivered 30% higher volumes than Season 1, and Peri-Peri delivered 30% higher volumes than Korean Season 2.
Navratri moved into Q2 this year; management said its impact was minimal given the veg/non-veg menu.
Indonesia tailwinds: boycott effects described as behind the company; green shoots seen over the last six weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Can restaurant EBITDA move from ~13% toward 15%, and what about double-digit company-level EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects EBITDA to hover above 13% and reach 15% through volume growth, with Families and kids programmes launching from November/December. New restaurants at lower ADS dilute SSSG.

qa_highlights.question: Will double-digit SSSG continue into Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to forecast, saying only that the quarter started very well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin plan, and what drove the dip?
qa_highlights.answer: The dip was attributed to a sudden chicken cost spike. Gross margin is expected to recover through DC-cluster distribution savings, scale purchasing, packaging and protein/vegetarian work. Current level of about 70.4-70.5% is considered a comfortable base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan to avoid repeating past rental and store-profitability mistakes as expansion accelerates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the team is unchanged, growth will be 'responsible' and linear, the pipeline is built 6-8 quarters ahead, and payback and return criteria apply to each site.

qa_highlights.question: How is excess capital from the primary raise being deployed, and what is the Indonesia primary infusion?
qa_highlights.answer: No capital allocation framework yet; a plan will come later with the promoters. The ₹130 crore Indonesia infusion is planned from the start of the year, will be tranched against milestones, and is for asset quality and losses.

qa_highlights.question: Will Burger King Indonesia resume store growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No; new-store growth is not an immediate priority until the asset-quality cycle completes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the return/ROCE framework for Indonesia?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is +₹5 million IDR daily ADS per restaurant from about ₹19-20 million, reaching about ₹25 million and a 15% restaurant EBITDA margin (pre-COVID ~27 million ADS and 15% margin).

risks_watch: Popeyes Indonesia remains loss-making at restaurant level; a resolution with the brand owner is pending.
Chicken and utility cost inflation; gross margin dipped ~0.4 points and recovery is 'unlikely to be linear'.
New restaurants at lower ADS and margins could dilute SSSG and EBITDA margin.
Indonesia recovery depends on Super Hemat traction and asset upgrades; October ADT data was not disclosed.
Capital deployment plan for the primary raise and warrants (~₹450 crore) is still undefined.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India trading and margins, with a high-level bias toward the outlook. Management was evasive on the Q3 SSSG and on the capital allocation plan, and it was cautious on Indonesia Popeyes, which it has not yet fixed.
key_quotes: We continue to grow through traffic, and that's the discipline of the first pillar that we have, which is value.

The target that that I had set with the with the team over there before I came in, full honest, you know, sharing with you, is is to improve every restaurant on a daily basis by 5 million IDR per day per restaurant.
So we are kind of going in with much more linear growth approach rather than the bulked-up growth approach towards towards the end of the quarter.

adds.what: India Burger King restaurant openings toward 80-100 per year in future (currently ~50-70/yr); 12 stores opened in October, 619 restaurants by call date

growth.why: Q2 consolidated revenue grew 20% and India SSSG was 14%, with India openings guided to rise toward 80-100 a year, backed by 619 restaurants open at call date and a pipeline built 6-8 quarters ahead; no numeric revenue growth guidance was given and Indonesia BK has no new store growth planned.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Restaurant EBITDA margin has hovered near 13% and management expects 15% via volume growth, though gross margin dipped ~0.4 pts to ~70.4-70.5% on chicken costs and recovery is 'unlikely to be linear'.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: India has 619 restaurants at call date (607 at quarter end), 12 opened in October, with openings guided to rise from ~50-70 a year toward 80-100 and a pipeline built 6-8 quarters ahead.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India SSSG 14% (prior quarter 12.6%) is traffic-led with 14 straight quarters of positive dine-in traffic, and India ADS held at ~Rs 1.31 lakh; management declined to forecast Q3/Q4 SSSG beyond a 'very good' start.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Indonesia asset upgrades (HVAC, kitchen, front-of-house) run ~6 months and up to Rs 130 crore primary capital is pending board approval, but no new India capex figure was given and India utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management was evasive on Q3/Q4 SSSG and gave no numeric revenue guidance, so an upgrade is hinted at but not guided.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Chicken cost inflation and new stores at lower ADS could dilute SSSG and margin, and Popeyes Indonesia (25 units, ADS down to Rs 64,000) remains loss-making.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Families and kids programmes launch from November/December, and Value programme 2 at Rs 79/99 is already on app, with Korean Season 2 volumes 30% above Season 1.

rows.label: Indonesia Burger King ADS and margin recovery
rows.why: Target of +5 million IDR daily ADS per restaurant from about 19-20 million to about 25 million, with a 15% restaurant EBITDA margin; Super Hemat added ~35-40 traffic per restaurant per day, and BK restaurant EBITDA was positive for three quarters.

rows.label: Indonesia primary infusion and warrant cash
rows.when: tranches tied to milestones, from start of year
rows.why: Up to Rs 130 crore for Indonesia is pending board approval and warrants could bring ~Rs 450 crore against ~Rs 1,000 crore liquidity, but no capital allocation framework exists yet.

rows.label: Popeyes Indonesia resolution with brand owner
rows.why: Restaurant EBITDA is weak across 25 Popeyes units with ADS down to Rs 64,000 and revenue ~Rs 15 crore; management is in talks with brand owners, with no timeline given.

tone.note: Management was confident on India traffic-led growth, margin path to 15%, and Indonesia ADS targets, but evasive on Q3/Q4 SSSG and capital allocation; analysts pushed on store-profitability risk from faster openings, gross margin recovery, and the excess primary capital plan.
